esgTreatment.title: Endoscopic Sleeve Gastroplasty (ESG)
esgTreatment.desc: ESG is a minimally invasive, non-surgical weight loss procedure that reduces the size of your stomach by up to 70-80% using an endoscopic suturing device inserted through the mouth. No incisions are required, making it ideal for patients with BMI 30-40 who prefer a non-surgical approach.
advantages: Shorter recovery time (return to normal activities in 1-3 days)
Lower complication risk compared to surgery
disadvantages: Less weight loss than surgical options like gastric sleeve
May require repeat procedures for optimal results
Relatively newer procedure with less long-term data

pose2Treatment.title: POSE-2 Double Helix
pose2Treatment.desc: POSE-2 (Primary Obesity Surgery Endoluminal) Double Helix is a minimally invasive, non-surgical weight loss procedure that reshapes the stomach using an endoscopic suturing platform inserted through the mouth — no incisions required. Full-thickness plications are placed in the stomach body, narrowing and shortening it by up to 70%, making it ideal for patients with BMI 30-40 who prefer a non-surgical approach.
advantages: Shorter recovery time (return to normal activities in 1-3 days)
Lower complication risk compared to surgery
disadvantages: Less weight loss than surgical options like gastric sleeve
May require repeat procedures for optimal results
Newer technique with fewer long-term studies than ESG

postBariatricSection.desc1: After significant weight loss following bariatric surgery, many patients are left with excess, sagging skin. Post-bariatric body contouring surgery removes this excess skin and reshapes the body to help you fully enjoy your transformation.
postBariatricSection.desc2: Our procedures include abdominoplasty (tummy tuck), arm lift, thigh lift, body lift, breast lift, and face/neck lift. These surgeries can dramatically improve body contour and eliminate skin irritation.

faqs.question: How much does weight loss surgery cost in Istanbul?
faqs.answer: All-inclusive packages at Istanbul Bariatric Center start from £1,650 for a gastric balloon, £2,950 for gastric sleeve, £3,350 for gastric bypass, and £4,950 for ESG. Every package covers your JCI-accredited hospital stay, pre-operative tests, VIP airport transfers, and dietitian follow-up.

faqs.question: Which bariatric procedure is right for me?
faqs.answer: The best procedure depends on your BMI, medical history, and weight-loss goals. Gastric sleeve suits BMI 35+, gastric bypass is recommended for BMI 40+ or patients with metabolic conditions, gastric balloon is a non-surgical option for BMI 30–40, and ESG offers a minimally invasive approach for BMI 30–40.

faqs.question: Is bariatric surgery at Istanbul Bariatric Center safe?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. All procedures are performed at JCI-accredited Liv Hospital in Istanbul by internationally trained surgeons. Dr Murat Ustun, the centre's founder and lead surgeon, has performed thousands of successful operations with outstanding safety outcomes.

faqs.question: What is included in each surgery package?
faqs.answer: Every package includes admission to a JCI-accredited hospital, full pre-operative testing, surgeon and anaesthesia fees, VIP airport transfer, and dietitian support. Relaxation and Luxury tiers add Dr Murat Ustun as your operating surgeon, extended hospital stays, Radisson hotel accommodation, UK-registered dietitian follow-up, and supplement packages.

faqs.question: How much weight can I expect to lose?
faqs.answer: Results vary by procedure: gastric sleeve patients typically lose 60–70% of excess weight, gastric bypass 70–80%, gastric balloon 10–15% of total body weight, and ESG 15–20% of total body weight — all within the first 12–18 months.

faqs.question: What is the recovery timeline?
faqs.answer: Gastric sleeve and bypass patients stay 2–3 days in hospital and return to daily activities within 2–3 weeks. Gastric balloon is a same-day procedure, and ESG patients can resume normal activities within 1–3 days.

faqs.question: Do I receive aftercare once I return home?
faqs.answer: Yes. Every patient receives a structured aftercare plan including dietitian guidance, follow-up consultations, and access to our UK-based patient-support team operating from 8 locations across the United Kingdom.

faqs.question: Who is Dr Murat Ustun?
faqs.answer: Dr Murat Ustun is the founder and lead bariatric surgeon at Istanbul Bariatric Center. A pioneer of ESG (Endoscopic Sleeve Gastroplasty) in Turkey, he has performed thousands of weight-loss procedures — including gastric sleeve, gastric bypass, and duodenal switch — at Liv Hospital in Istanbul.

gastricSleeve.title: Gastric Sleeve Surgery
gastricSleeve.heroSubtitle: Gastric sleeve surgery is one of the most applied bariatric surgeries both worldwide and in Turkey. Discover why it's so effective.
gastricSleeve.desc: Also known as sleeve gastrectomy, this procedure involves removing 70-80% of the stomach, leaving a tubular pouch. It restricts food intake and impacts gut hormones to reduce hunger.
gastricSleeve.overviewP1: Gastric sleeve or sleeve gastrectomy is a bariatric surgery that is performed by cutting a part of your stomach to create a smaller chamber. It is one of the most applied bariatric surgeries both worldwide and Turkey.
gastricSleeve.overviewP2: Obesity is one of the most annoying problems for many people around the world, not just because of the changing in shape, face, or body that comes after it, but also because of the health problems that can be caused by it.
gastricSleeve.overviewP3: There are several diseases that are directly related to obesity such as: Diabetes type II, High blood pressure, Heart problems, High Cholesterol and More.
advantages: Controls amount of food held in stomach
risks: Bleeding from the inside of the stomach or the surgical wound.
Deep Vein Thrombosis: or DVT which is blood clot forming in your vein during the procedure or during the recovery process.
Irregular heartbeat: some surgeries can lead to an irregular heartbeat during the surgery.
Gastric Leaks: the stomach fluids can leak from the suture line in your stomach.
Stenosis: which means that a part of your stomach might close causing an obstruction in your stomach.
Vitamin deficiency: the removed part of your stomach is partially responsible for vitamin absorption.

gastricBypass.title: Gastric Bypass Surgery
gastricBypass.heroSubtitle: Mini gastric bypass is a simplified version of the traditional gastric bypass, offering excellent weight loss results with fewer complications.
gastricBypass.desc: The stomach is divided into two parts, creating a smaller pouch. The small intestine is rearranged to connect to both. This limits food intake and calorie absorption.
gastricBypass.tocItem1: How can mini gastric bypass surgery help me lose weight?
gastricBypass.tocItem2: Are there any side effects for mini gastric bypass surgery?
gastricBypass.tocItem3: Do insurance companies cover the fees of the surgery?
gastricBypass.tocItem4: Things You Need to Know Before Mini Gastric Bypass Surgery
gastricBypass.introP1: For many people around the world, excess weight and obesity is a very serious problem not just because of the changing in shape, face, or body that comes after it, but also because of the health problem that can be caused by it.
gastricBypass.introP2: In fact, obesity is a very important reason and might be the direct reason for most of the strokes, blood sugar, blood pressure problems, breathing problems, stomach problems, and many other health problems.
gastricBypass.introP3: There are several types for weight loss surgery each one differs from the other in its steps but all of them share the same pleasant results which is significant weight loss. One of these types is called mini gastric sleeve bypass.
gastricBypass.introP4: This surgery is considered to be one of the most effective weight loss surgeries and has many advantages compared to other types of weight loss surgery.
gastricBypass.introP5: Just like any other weight loss surgery, the basic idea of mini gastric surgery is to reduce the volume of the stomach to decrease the amount of food consumed by the patient. However, the mini gastric bypass surgery involves different steps. During the surgery, the doctor will cut the upper part of the stomach and divide it into a tube, and then join it to a loop of intestine. The rest of the stomach which equals 75% of the entire stomach will remain useless.
gastricBypass.introP6: The top of the stomach is stapled to form a 50 ml size tube, this tube will be the new small stomach and completely separated from the original stomach. This stomach is then sewn to a loop of the small intestine, bypassing the first part of the intestine called the duodenum and approximately 150–200cm of the bowel.
gastricBypass.introP7: The mini gastric bypass surgery can be used as a primary weight loss surgery or can be used for people who already tried diet and daily exercises but did not have any pleasant results, or for patients who are redoing a weight loss surgery because the first one did not succeed for any reason.
gastricBypass.howItHelpsTitle: Mini Gastric Bypass: Expected Weight Loss & Health Benefits
gastricBypass.howItHelpsIntro: The mini gastric bypass surgery helps you lose weight in several ways:
gastricBypass.benefit1Desc: The removed part of the stomach is responsible for hunger hormone. Thus, when it is removed the feeling for hunger will be reduced which will result in less weight.
gastricBypass.benefit2Desc: By reducing the amount of food entering the stomach as the volume of your stomach has become smaller after the surgery.
gastricBypass.benefit3Desc: By reducing the amount of calories you absorb from the food you eat which results in a healthier lifestyle.
gastricBypass.additionalBenefitsDesc: After two years you will lose around 80% of your weight, and serious health problems and diseases like type 2 diabetes, blood sugar diseases, heart problems will be improved or even disappear after doing this surgery.
gastricBypass.sideEffectsTitle: Are there any side effects for mini gastric bypass surgery?
gastricBypass.sideEffectsIntro: Well just like any other surgery in any other field there are some side effects that might happen during the surgery or after the surgery. Despite that the mini gastric bypass surgery is safe but still there are some risks that we can mention:
sideEffects: Bleeding from inside your stomach or your stomach wound.
You might feel pain if the doctor or medical team did not give you powerful general anesthesia.
Gastric Leaks: the stomach fluids can leak from the suture line in your stomach.
Stenosis: which means that a part of your stomach might close causing an obstruction in your stomach.
Vitamin deficiency: the removed part of your stomach is partially responsible for vitamin absorption so when you lose this part, the vitamins in your body will decrease.
gastricBypass.sideEffectsConclusion: These risks are considered to be early complications and thankfully 95% of the cases are successful. Still, there are some late complications that might appear like Internal hernia despite that the risk of internal hernia is considerably lower after mini-bypass than after standard gastric bypass. Sometimes the loops of bowel in the abdomen can become entangled and get stuck. In this case, another operation or surgery is necessary to fix the problem.
gastricBypass.insuranceTitle: Do insurance companies cover the fees of the surgery?
gastricBypass.insuranceDesc: Most insurance companies cover the surgery costs if the patient accomplishes BMI Index condition. Of course, this information changes from a country to another one so it is better to ask about this information in your country.
gastricBypass.thingsToKnowTitle: Things You Need to Know Before Mini Gastric Bypass Surgery
thingsToKnow: Patients who would like to have this surgery should score at least 35 kg/m² in BMI index.
A patient will spend an hour to 90 minutes in the hospital doing the surgery.
A patient must stay at the hospital for three to four days to make sure that nothing is going wrong.
A patient will lose between 70% to 85% of the overall weight.
A patient must know that the sickness will go after three weeks at maximum.
A patient must take supplements for life-long time.
A patient must follow the doctor's instructions and given diets.
gastricBypass.thingsToKnowConclusion: In the end, you should know that despite being safe and not very hard but the doctor or the medical team should know all the information related to your health stature including your medical history report just to avoid any problems whether during the surgery or after the surgery during the recovery time.

gastricBypass.ctaDesc: Contact us today for a free consultation and learn how mini gastric bypass surgery can help you achieve your weight loss goals.

duodenalSwitch.title: Duodenal Switch
duodenalSwitch.heroSubtitle: One of the most effective weight loss surgeries for patients with severe obesity, offering significant and lasting results.
duodenalSwitch.desc: A complex procedure combining sleeve gastrectomy with intestinal bypass. It offers the most significant weight loss but carries higher risks.
duodenalSwitch.introP1: Nowadays there are many people around the world complaining of obesity problems, especially that it is responsible for many serious health problems like heartbreaks, strokes, liver and kidney problems, and many more health issues. Thus, hundreds of thousands of people who complain of obesity started to have obesity surgeries.
duodenalSwitch.introP2: There are several types for obesity surgery, each type has its own tools and way to be done but all of the types share the same goal which is helping to cure obesity problems.
duodenalSwitch.introP3: Duodenal switch surgery is one of the obesity surgery types and a very efficient one.

faqs.question: What is Duodenal Switch surgery?
faqs.answer: Or as some doctors call it "Gastric Reduction Duodenal Switch" is a weight loss surgery that involves both restrictive and malabsorptive aspects. The restrictive part of the surgery involves cutting up to 70% of the stomach and some of the duodenum.

faqs.question: Is it similar to gastric bypass?
faqs.answer: The duodenal switch is similar to gastric bypass in goals because it reduces the amount of food entering your stomach and reduces the amount of calories absorbed to your body, but because it is more of malabsorptive operation, it causes more side effects than other types of surgeries.

faqs.question: Is duodenal switch better than other types of obesity surgery?
faqs.answer: Some doctors suggest that it is better for the long term because in duodenal switch the stomach will remain big so it will host more food compared to the other types of obesity surgery, this will help you having better body shape in the long term.

faqs.question: Can anyone have the duodenal switch surgery? How do I know if I'm a candidate?
faqs.answer: Not anyone can have duodenal switch surgery, only the doctor or medical team can decide that and the decision will be according to your BMI "Body Mass Index" if it is greater than 40 then you can have the duodenal switch surgery. Of course, there are other things to take in consideration so it is very important that your doctor decide whether you can have the duodenal switch surgery or not.

faqs.question: How long is the recovery time for duodenal switch surgery?
faqs.answer: It differs from one patient to another but for most patients it needs between three to four weeks of recovery. Even though that the surgery does not leave many scars from outside but it requires hard work from the inside.

faqs.question: Can I get back to work after the recovery time and start exercising?
faqs.answer: It is better to take another week away from the stress and hard activities just to make sure that your body has adjusted to the new situation after the surgery.

faqs.question: How long does it take for me to lose weight after the surgery?
faqs.answer: Most patients who have had the duodenal switch surgery lose their weight during the first 12 to 18 months. This is why not everyone feels encouraged to have this type of obesity surgery.

faqs.question: Is it possible that I gain weight after losing it?
faqs.answer: Well it can be if you get back to the old unhealthy lifestyle but it is known about duodenal surgery that it has the best long lasting weight loss among the obesity surgery types.

faqs.question: Do I have to avoid certain kinds of food after the surgery?
faqs.answer: It is hard to tell specific types of food because it differs from one patient to another but there are some types of food that you should absolutely stay away from like fatty food because it causes diarrhea. In any case it is important to take the answers of this question from the doctor after he or she examines your body.

faqs.question: How much weight will I lose after the surgery?
faqs.answer: Most patients lose between 40 to 60% of their weight. However, you need to know that none of this will happen if you don't put in an extra effort and change your lifestyle to a healthier one.

faqs.question: Does duodenal switch surgery prevent pregnancy? Or have any negative effects on pregnant bodies?
faqs.answer: The surgery will not prevent pregnancy. However, during the first 18 months we suggest that a woman do not experience pregnancy because during this time she will be losing weight and this might affect negatively on her body. In any case, weight loss surgeries help women in having a healthier pregnancy experience (after the maximum loss of weight).

faqs.question: Does duodenal switch surgery cost more than other obesity surgeries?
faqs.answer: It costs a little bit more than other types of obesity surgery because it requires more work and effort from the medical team and surgeons.

duodenalSwitch.diabetesP1: Duodenal switch surgery is particularly effective for patients with Type 2 diabetes. The procedure not only helps with significant weight loss but also has been shown to improve or even resolve diabetes in many patients.
duodenalSwitch.diabetesP2: The malabsorptive component of the surgery changes how the body processes food and can lead to improved insulin sensitivity and blood sugar control. Many patients see improvements in their diabetes even before significant weight loss occurs.
duodenalSwitch.diabetesHighlight: Studies have shown that duodenal switch has one of the highest rates of diabetes remission among all bariatric procedures, making it an excellent choice for patients with severe obesity complicated by diabetes.

hero.title: Revision Bariatric Surgery in Turkey
hero.subtitle: Weight regain after a gastric sleeve or bypass is more common than you think — and it is fixable. Explore surgical and non-surgical revision pathways with one of Turkey's most experienced revision teams.

why.title: Why Weight Loss Surgery Sometimes Needs a Second Step
why.p1: No bariatric operation guarantees permanent results on its own. Over time, a gastric sleeve can gradually stretch, the outlet after a gastric bypass can widen, and hormonal adaptation can bring hunger back. Studies show that up to 30% of sleeve patients experience significant weight regain within five years, and severe acid reflux (GERD) develops in as many as 55% of sleeve patients over the long term.
why.p2: None of this means your first surgery "failed you" — it means your anatomy and metabolism have changed, and there is a well-established medical pathway to correct it. Revision bariatric surgery restores the restriction and metabolic effect of your original procedure, or converts it to one that suits your body better.
why.p3: At Istanbul Bariatric Center, every revision starts with a diagnostic work-up — endoscopy and imaging — so the pathway is chosen based on why the first operation stopped working, not guesswork.

pathways.title: Revision Pathways Compared
pathways.subtitle: The right revision depends on your original procedure, your symptoms, and your goals.
rows: Weight regain after sleeve, especially with reflux (GERD)
Converts the sleeve into a small pouch connected to the intestine, resolving reflux and adding a metabolic effect
High BMI or type 2 diabetes after a sleeve
Keeps the sleeve and adds an intestinal component for maximum weight loss and diabetes control
Moderately stretched sleeve, patients wanting to avoid surgery
Endoscopic sutures through the mouth re-tighten the stretched sleeve — no incisions
Weight regain after gastric bypass due to a stretched stoma
Endoscopic sutures narrow the widened outlet between pouch and intestine
Removes the band and converts to a sleeve or bypass in one or two stages

candidacy.title: Are You a Candidate for Revision Surgery?
candidacy.intro: You may benefit from a revision assessment if any of the following apply:
criteria: You regained a significant portion of the weight you lost after sleeve, bypass, or band surgery
You never reached your expected weight loss after the first operation
You developed severe or persistent acid reflux (GERD) after a gastric sleeve
You feel hungry soon after meals or can eat much larger portions than before
You have a gastric band causing discomfort, slippage, or inadequate results
Your type 2 diabetes returned or was never fully resolved after surgery
candidacy.note: Important: revision surgery is more technically demanding than primary surgery. Choose a high-volume centre with specific revision experience — surgeon expertise is the single biggest factor in revision outcomes.

process.title: How the Revision Process Works at IBC
steps: Free remote assessment. Share your surgical history, current weight and symptoms with our coordinators on WhatsApp. Dr Murat Ustun reviews every revision case personally.
Diagnostic work-up in Istanbul. On arrival, you undergo endoscopy, imaging and blood tests at JCI-accredited Liv Hospital to establish exactly why the first procedure stopped working.
Pathway decision. Based on the findings, the team recommends the least invasive option that will reliably meet your goals — endoscopic where possible, surgical where needed.
Procedure and recovery. Endoscopic revisions are usually same-day; surgical conversions involve 2–3 nights in hospital plus hotel recovery with our team nearby.
12 months of aftercare. UK-registered dietitian support, supplement guidance and regular follow-ups protect your second-chance result.
process.readMore: Read more in our in-depth guides: <guideRevision>Revisional Bariatric Surgery in Turkey</guideRevision> and <guideTore>the TORe procedure explained</guideTore>.

items.question: What is revision bariatric surgery?
items.answer: Revision bariatric surgery is a second procedure performed after a previous weight loss operation — such as gastric sleeve, gastric bypass, or gastric band — when the first surgery has led to weight regain, insufficient weight loss, or complications such as severe reflux. The revision pathway is chosen based on your anatomy, symptoms and goals.

items.question: How much weight regain is normal after gastric sleeve?
items.answer: Some weight fluctuation is normal, but studies show that up to 30% of sleeve patients experience significant weight regain within 5 years, often due to gradual stretching of the sleeve or hormonal adaptation. If you have regained more than 25% of the weight you originally lost, a revision assessment is worthwhile.

items.question: Which revision procedure is best after a failed gastric sleeve?
items.answer: The most common options are conversion to mini gastric bypass (especially when reflux is present — GERD affects up to 55% of sleeve patients long-term), conversion to duodenal switch or transit bipartition for greater metabolic effect, or a non-surgical endoscopic re-sleeve. The right option depends on why the sleeve failed, which is assessed with endoscopy and imaging.

items.question: Can a gastric bypass be revised without surgery?
items.answer: Yes. If the connection between pouch and intestine (the stoma) has stretched, TORe (Transoral Outlet Reduction) tightens it endoscopically through the mouth — no incisions, usually same-day discharge. It is the leading non-surgical revision for weight regain after bypass.

items.question: Is revision bariatric surgery riskier than the first surgery?
items.answer: Revision surgery is technically more complex because of scar tissue from the first operation, which is why surgeon experience matters more than for primary surgery. In high-volume centres with experienced revision surgeons, complication rates remain low and outcomes are excellent.

Every quote includes JCI-accredited hospital stay, pre-operative endoscopy and tests, transfers, hotel and aftercare. Contact us for a personalised assessment and exact quote.

whyCheaper.p1: The price difference is not about lower standards. Turkey has one of the largest medical-tourism sectors in the world, and Istanbul's leading hospitals hold the same JCI (Joint Commission International) accreditation as top hospitals in London, New York and Berlin.
factors: Operating costs: staff, facility and administrative costs in Turkey are a fraction of Western levels, without affecting clinical equipment or protocols.
Exchange rate: your pound, euro or dollar goes significantly further in Turkey.
Volume and specialisation: high-volume bariatric centres like ours achieve efficiencies — and better outcomes — that low-volume clinics cannot.
whyCheaper.p3: Dr Murat Ustun has performed over 8,000 bariatric procedures — a caseload very few Western surgeons ever accumulate. With surgery, volume is one of the strongest predictors of safety.

items.question: Why is weight loss surgery so much cheaper in Turkey?
items.answer: The difference is driven by lower operating costs, a favourable exchange rate, and government support for medical tourism — not lower standards. Surgery is performed at JCI-accredited hospitals (the same international accreditation held by top US and European hospitals) by high-volume surgeons. You pay 60-70% less for the same clinical standard.

items.question: Are there any hidden costs in the packages?

The only costs not included are your flights and personal spending.

items.question: How does the cost compare to the UK, US, or Europe?
items.answer: A gastric sleeve costs around £10,000–£15,000 privately in the UK, $16,000–$25,000 in the US, and €8,000–€12,000 in much of Western Europe. In Istanbul the equivalent all-inclusive package is £2,950–£4,250 — typically a 60–75% saving even after flights.

items.question: Can I pay in instalments or with finance?
items.answer: Payment is normally made by bank transfer or card, with a deposit to secure your date and the balance on arrival. Speak to our coordinators about currently available payment arrangements for your country.

items.question: Does travel insurance or the NHS cover surgery in Turkey?
items.answer: The NHS and standard travel insurance do not cover planned surgery abroad. However, specialist medical-travel insurance covering complications is available and we recommend it. Many patients still find the total cost — surgery, flights, hotel, and insurance — far below a private operation at home.

items.question: Is it safe for UK patients to have weight loss surgery in Turkey?
items.answer: Yes — when you choose the right provider. Istanbul Bariatric Center operates exclusively at JCI-accredited Liv Hospital, the same international accreditation standard held by leading UK private hospitals. Dr Murat Ustun has performed over 8,000 procedures and the centre has won the WhatClinic Patient Service Award six times. The key is verifying hospital accreditation and surgeon volume before you book — with any provider.

items.question: How long do I need to stay in Istanbul?
items.answer: Most UK patients stay 4-6 nights in total: arrival and pre-operative tests on day one, surgery on day two, 2-3 nights in hospital, then 1-2 nights at the hotel before flying home. ESG and gastric balloon patients can often return home within 2-3 days.

items.question: What aftercare do I get back in the UK?
items.answer: Relaxation and Luxury packages include 12 months of support from a UK-registered dietitian, plus care support coordinators in 8 UK locations for in-person help. Our clinical team remains available on WhatsApp for any concern, and we coordinate with your GP where needed.

items.question: Will the NHS look after me if something goes wrong?
items.answer: The NHS will always treat you in an emergency. For routine follow-up, our UK dietitian network and remote clinical team handle your aftercare. We also strongly recommend specialist medical-travel insurance, which covers complication treatment — policies typically cost £100-£200.

items.question: How do payments work from the UK?
items.answer: You pay a deposit by card or bank transfer to secure your surgery date, with the balance payable on arrival in Istanbul. All prices are quoted in pounds sterling and fixed — the quote you receive is the amount you pay.

items.question: Do I need a visa to travel to Turkey from the UK?
items.answer: No. UK passport holders can enter Turkey visa-free for up to 90 days. You only need a passport valid for at least 150 days from your arrival date, plus your booking confirmation from us.
